newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota wheat stressed by hot, dry weather.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota wheat stressed by hot, dry weather.

text.p: Hot, dry weather stressed North Dakota's wheat and other crops during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
"Condition of all crops except sugarbeets deteriorated during the week," the report said. "Dry soil conditions continue to hinder crop development and pasture growth."

Spring wheat was 99 percent planted, ahead of 94 last week, 93 last year and the five-year average of 95 percent. Spring wheat condition was rated 66 percent good to excellent, 25 percent fair and nine percent poor.
Barley condition was rated 10 percent excellent, 57 good, 24 fair, eight poor and one very poor. Durum condition was rated two percent excellent, 45 good, 33 fair, 17 poor and three very poor.
Durum wheat planted 98 pct vs 92 w/a, 93 y/a, 95 avge.
Oats planted 100 pct vs 96 w/a, 94 y/a, 95 avge.
Barley planted 99 pct vs 93 w/a, 95 y/a, 96 avge.
Corn planted 98 pct vs 93 w/a, 93 y/a, 95 avge.
Soybeans planted 95 pct vs 72 w/a, 77 y/a, 90 avge.
Sugarbeets planted 100 pct vs 99 w/a, 98 y/a, 100 avge.
Sunflowers planted 13 pct vs 1 w/a, 1 y/a, 19 avge.
